title: Microfluidic Synthesis of Microgel Building Blocks for Microporous Annealed Particle Scaffold
protocol: Add 1 g of 4-arm 20 kDa PEG-maleimide to 10 mL of 1x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.4) in a small glass beaker with a stir bar.
Stir the solution at 300 rpm until the PEG is fully dissolved (~30 min).
Add 146.5 µL of 2-aminoethanethiol solution to the reaction and stir at 300 rpm for 1 h and 10 min.
Mix 160.1 mg of DMTMM and 32.77 µL of methacrylic acid in 5 mL of 1x PBS (pH 7.4) in a new glass beaker.
React the mixture with stirring at 300 rpm for 50 min.
Add methacrylic acid to the PEG-MAL/2-aminoethanethiol solution.
Add DMTMM to the beaker containing the PEG and amine compounds.
Add triethylamine (at a 1:1 molar ratio to methacrylic acid) to the reaction mixture.
Stir the reaction overnight at 300 rpm with the beaker covered in foil.
Transfer the reaction to snakeskin dialysis tubing with a molecular weight cut-off of 3,500 Da.
Place the dialysis tubing in a large beaker with 1 M NaCl in deionized water.
Stir the solution at 300 rpm for 3 days.
Change the 1 M NaCl solution twice daily for six washes.
Dialyze in DI water for 6 hours.
Change the DI water each hour for six washes.
Transfer the reaction to a 50 mL conical tube.
Freeze the tube at -80 °C.
Lyophilize the tube for at least 72 hours starting from -70 °C with a temperature ramp of 0.01 °C/min until 0 °C.
Dissolve 25 mg of MethMAL in 700 µL of chloroform-d.
Transfer the solution to an NMR tube.
Acquire the 1H-NMR spectra.
Integrate the maleimide peak as a reference (~6.76 ppm).
Integrate the two methacrylamide peaks (~5.35 ppm and 5.6 ppm).
Divide the ratio of the methacrylamide peak areas by the total area of all three peaks to obtain the percentage of arms modified with methacrylamide.
Predetermine the desired concentrations of polymer, crosslinker, and other gel precursor components.
Dissolve PEG-MAL in 10x PBS (pH 1.5).
Dissolve RGD in 10x PBS (pH 1.5).
Dissolve MethMAL in 10x PBS (pH 1.5).
Dissolve MMP-2 crosslinker in 1x PBS (pH 7.4).
Prepare a viscometer with a gap size of 0.4 mm.
Attach a 35 mm plate rotor geometry.
Maintain a humidified environment around the geometry.
Mix PEG-backbone and MMP-crosslinker in a 1:1 volumetric ratio.
Pipette 400 μL of the gel precursor solution onto the center of the viscometer stage.
Lower the geometry to reach a gap size of 0.4 mm.
Monitor storage (G') and loss (G'') moduli for up to 6 h at room temperature.
Create the first polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) microfluidic device from an SU-8 wafer photomask.
Prepare ~200 g of PDMS by mixing the base and curing agent in a 10:1 w/w ratio.
Place the SU-8 wafer in a culture dish, taping the edges to secure it.
Pour PDMS into the dish to create a 1-1.5 cm thick layer over the wafer.
Place the dish under vacuum to remove any bubbles.
Let the PDMS cure until solidified (24 h at room temperature or ~2 h at 60 °C).
Cut a rectangle through the cured PDMS with a 0.5-1 cm margin around the design on the wafer.
Wedge a spatula into one of the cuts and slide it along the cuts to separate the PDMS from the wafer.
Lift the rectangle of PDMS out of the dish using the spatula as an air bubble forms under the PDMS.
Mix ~15-20 g of PDMS in a 10:1 ratio of base to curing agent.
Pour the mixed PDMS into the rectangular gap in the mold to create a 5 mm layer above the wafer.
Place the mold under vacuum to remove any bubbles from the PDMS.
Let the PDMS cure for 24 hours at room temperature or 2 hours at 60 °C until fully solidified.
Use a razor blade or scalpel to cut around the edges of the rectangle in the cured PDMS layer.
Use a 1.5 mm biopsy punch to create holes at the inlets and outlet of the PDMS rectangle.
Score the PDMS between each device on a single wafer using a spatula or razor blade.
Gently fold the scored PDMS along the lines for clean separation.
Store separated PDMS devices in a dust-free container.
Prepare one glass slide per PDMS microfluidic device.
Remove dust from the glass slides using tape, filtered air, or isopropyl alcohol (IPA) washes.
Ensure the slides are completely dry before proceeding to the next step.
Place a glass slide and a PDMS device design-side up on a small plastic tray.
Insert the tray into a plasma cleaner and close the door and air-flow valve.
Turn on the vacuum pump and run for at least 30 seconds, then turn off.
Connect the oxygen tank gas tube to the air-flow valve and let it fill with oxygen for 30 seconds.
Close the air-flow valve and turn off the oxygen supply.
Set the radiofrequency (RF) level to high and wait until the chamber turns a violet-pink color.
Allow 30 seconds after reaching the violet-pink color before turning off the plasma and vacuum.
Slowly open the air-flow valve to release the vacuum.
Remove the tray from the plasma cleaner.
Gently flip the PDMS device onto the glass slide to bond them.
Observe the slight difference in transparency of the PDMS during bonding.
Store the bonded devices at 60°C until immediately before use.
Prepare the surface treatment by diluting PFOCTS (trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl)silane) in Novec oil at a ratio of 1:50.
Use 1 mL of diluted solution for 3-4 devices.
Transfer the surface treatment volume to a 1 mL syringe and attach a 25 G needle.
Cut a 10-12 cm piece of Tygon tubing per device that will be treated.
Insert a couple of millimeters of PEEK tubing into the end of Tygon tubing.
Take the device(s) out of the heated chamber.
Insert the non-PEEK end of the Tygon tubing into the aqueous inlet hole.
Insert the needle of the surface treatment syringe into the PEEK tubing and cover the oil chamber outlet hole.
Inject the treatment slowly to ensure filling without bubbles.
Wait for the aqueous chambers to fill first, followed by smaller channels, then the oil chamber.
Remove the Tygon tubing from the device once filled.
Let the treated device rest for 10 min at room temperature.
Fill a 5 mL syringe with oil only.
Attach a 25 G needle to the syringe.
Aspirate the surface treatment out of the device through the inlets and outlet.
Insert Tygon tubing into the aqueous inlet.
Insert the syringe with oil into the PEEK tubing.
Flush each device with oil.
Aspirate the oil out of the device.
Repeat the oil flush two more times.
Remove the Tygon tubing.
Prepare 6 mL of surfactant solution by diluting the stock 5% FluoroSurfactant to at least 1% in Novec oil.
Add the surfactant solution to a 10 mL syringe.
Cut three pieces of Tygon tubing appropriate for the syringe pump height.
Cut two pieces of PEEK tubing, approximately 1 inch in length.
Insert a couple of millimeters of PEEK tubing into the end of two Tygon tubing pieces.
Insert the non-PEEK end of the Tygon tubing into the inlets of the microfluidic devices.
Insert the remaining piece of Tygon tubing (without PEEK) into the outlet of the microfluidic device.
Add at least 3 mL of oil to a 5 mL plastic syringe and attach it to a 25 G needle.
Carefully insert the needle into the PEEK tubing on one of the Tygon inlets.
Gently flush the tubing and device with oil.
Collect the oil from the outlet in a conical tube.
Repeat the oil flush on the other Tygon inlet.
Set the syringe pumps to a flow rate of 3 mL/h for aqueous flow and 6 mL/h for oil flow.
Connect the syringe containing surfactant to the oil inlet via a 25 G needle.
Gently dispense enough oil to prime tubing and the oil channel of the microfluidic device.
Add 0.5 mL of oil to a new 5 mL syringe that will contain the gel precursor.
In a conical tube, combine 1.5 mL of PEG-backbone solution with 1.5 mL of crosslinker solution.
Vortex the combined gel precursor solution for 30 seconds.
Quickly transfer the combined gel precursor to the 5 mL syringe.
Connect the syringe with gel precursor to the aqueous inlet via a 25 G needle.
Gently dispense enough solution to prime tubing and the aqueous channel.
Clamp the syringes onto respective syringe pumps and press run.
Ensure liquid is flowing through both aqueous and oil channels.
Visualize microgel formation within PDMS device using a microscope.
Collect uniform-sized particles from the outlet in a conical tube.
Use a pipette to carefully remove the oil phase from the bottom of the tube once gelation is complete.
Deposit the removed oil into an appropriate waste container for fluorinated waste.
Add more oil into the microgel collection tube in a 1:1 ratio with the existing contents.
Mix by gently inverting the collection tube.
Let the collection tube settle for ~5 min to allow phase separation.
Remove oil phase from the bottom of the tube with a pipette and discard.
Add more oil at a 1:1 ratio with the gel, then add 1x PBS in a 4:1 ratio with the gel volume.
Invert the tube several times to mix thoroughly.
Centrifuge the tube at ~2,000 x g for ~30 s to separate layers.
Remove the oil phase from the bottom of the tube with a pipette and discard.
Repeat oil and PBS washes 2x more as described previously.
Check for the gel transitioning from opaque to clear after final wash, indicating surfactant removal.
In a chemical fume hood, add hexanes at an equal volume to the PBS.
Vortex the conical tube thoroughly for 30 s or until mixed well.
Centrifuge at 4,696 x g for 5 min to separate layers.
Remove and discard the hexane layer from the top of the tube.
Aspirate the PBS layer.
Repeat hexane and PBS washes at least 2x more or until the gel appears nearly translucent.
Wash the gel with PBS once to remove any remaining hexanes.
Centrifuge at 4,696 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the PBS layer without disturbing the gel pellet.
Prepare a 100 mM solution of N-acetyl-L-cysteine in 1x PBS.
Add this quenching solution to the gel and place on a tube rotator at 37 °C overnight.
Wash the microgels extensively with PBS to remove unreacted N-acetyl-L-cysteine.
For long-term storage, resuspend the microgels in 70% IPA and store at 4 °C for up to 1 year.
Add 70% IPA to the gel in a 4:1 v/v ratio in a biosafety hood.
Vortex the tube for 30 s and centrifuge at 4,696 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the IPA supernatant from the gel pellet in a biosafety hood.
Perform two more IPA washes followed by three PBS washes.
Ensure all IPA is removed before using the microgels with cells or animals.
Allow microgel particles to equilibrate in 1x PBS overnight at 37°C to swell to their final diameter before sizing.
Spin down the MAP gel at 4,696 × g for 5 min and aspirate the supernatant.
Remove 5 μL of microgels from the gel pellet using a positive displacement pipette.
Dilute in 1 mL of PBS in a microcentrifuge tube (1:200 dilution).
Transfer 100 µL of the diluted microgels to the wells of a clear 96-well plate.
Visualize the microgels with a widefield or confocal microscope using a 10x objective.
Acquire images of the microgels for analysis.
Analyze particles using Analyze | Analyze Particles.
Enter the area size range in pixel^2 for microgels to exclude small debris.
Change circularity filter settings to 0.75-1.00.
Select Show | Outlines to display outlines of analyzed particles.
Check Display Results and Exclude on Edges options.
Run the Analyze Particles module.
Wait for output, which includes Feret's diameter of each particle.
Export results to a spreadsheet.
Calculate polydispersity index (PDI) using equations (2), (3), and (4).
Analyze at least 100 microgels to define population characteristics.
Create a stock solution of 2 mM lithium phenyl-2,4,6-trimethylbenzoylphosphinate in 1x PBS (pH 7.4).
Dilute the LAP stock solution to 0.2 mM in a volume of 1x PBS equivalent to the gel volume.
Sterilize the LAP solution before use for cell or animal studies.
Spin down the MAP gel at 4,696 × g for 5 min and aspirate the supernatant.
Transfer the desired volume of gel into a microcentrifuge tube using a positive displacement pipette.
Add 0.2 mM LAP to the gel in a 1:1 volumetric ratio (final LAP concentration is 0.1 mM).
Vortex the mixture and incubate for at least 15 min in the dark.
Centrifuge the mixture at 18,000 × g for 5 min to pellet the gel.
Carefully remove the supernatant from the gel pellet.
Transfer the MAP gel to the target location with a positive displacement pipette.
Apply focused light (365 nm, 8.66 mW/cm²) to the sample for 113 s to anneal the scaffold.
